digest.lead: Anthropic is reportedly heading toward its first profitable quarter driven by 'mind-blowing growth', while expanding infrastructure with GB200 chips on Colossus2.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, Claude Code v2.1.146 ships with improved code review commands and Windows fixes, and the community continues exploring AI-assisted development workflows.

stories.headline: Anthropic Approaching First Profitable Quarter Amid Infrastructure Expansion
stories.summary: Anthropic is reportedly on track for its first profitable quarter driven by significant revenue growth [1]. The company is simultaneously expanding its infrastructure by moving to Colossus2 with GB200 chips [2].
key_points: Revenue growth described as 'mind-blowing' by WSJ report
Infrastructure expansion includes deployment of NVIDIA GB200 chips
Move to Colossus2 represents major scaling of compute capacity
stories.impact: This milestone signals Anthropic's transition from research startup to sustainable AI company, potentially affecting competitive dynamics in the LLM market and enterprise AI adoption.

sources.title: Mind-Blowing Growth Is About to Propel Anthropic into First Profitable Quarter
Anthropic is expanding to Colossus2. Will use GB200

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.146 Improves Code Review Commands and Fixes Windows Issues
stories.summary: Claude Code's latest update renames the `/simplify` command to `/code-review` with optional effort levels and fixes several bugs including Windows PowerShell compatibility issues [1]. The release also resolves MCP pagination problems and screen rendering issues.
key_points: New `/code-review` command replaces `/simplify` with configurable effort levels
Fixes Windows PowerShell tool failures when pwsh is installed via winget or Microsoft Store
Resolves MCP pagination issues that were dropping items beyond page 1
stories.impact: These improvements make Claude Code more reliable for Windows developers and provide better code review workflows for teams using the CLI tool daily.

stories.headline: Developer Shares Insights from 100,000 Lines of Rust Code Written with AI
stories.summary: A detailed retrospective examines the experience of writing 100K lines of Rust code using AI assistance, including Claude Code, covering lessons learned about spec-driven development and AI-assisted programming workflows [1]. The post has generated significant discussion in the developer community.
key_points: Covers practical experiences with AI-assisted Rust development at scale
Discusses spec-driven development approaches when working with AI
Provides real-world insights into AI coding tool effectiveness
stories.impact: This retrospective offers valuable guidance for developers considering AI-assisted development workflows, particularly those working with systems programming languages like Rust.

sources.title: Learnings from 100K lines of Rust with AI (2025)

stories.headline: Use `/code-review` with effort levels for better code analysis
stories.summary: The `/simplify` command has been renamed to `/code-review` and now accepts optional effort levels like 'high' for more thorough analysis. This gives you better control over how deeply Claude examines your code for potential improvements.
actionable_steps: Add effort levels like `/code-review high` for more thorough analysis
Use `/code-review low` for quick reviews or `/code-review medium` for standard analysis

stories.headline: Use _meta annotation to prevent large MCP tool results from being truncated
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports preserving large tool results (like database schemas) up to 500K characters by adding a special metadata annotation. This prevents important data from being cut off during processing.
actionable_steps: Add `_meta["anthropic/maxResultSizeChars"]` annotation to your MCP tool result
Set the value to your desired character limit (up to 500,000)
Test with large results like database schemas to verify they pass through completely

stories.headline: Use case-insensitive agent type names in Claude Code configurations
stories.summary: Claude Code now accepts agent type names with any casing and separators. This makes configuration more flexible and reduces errors from formatting inconsistencies.
actionable_steps: In your Claude Code configuration, use any casing for agent types (e.g., 'Code Reviewer', 'code-reviewer', 'CODE_REVIEWER')
Test that your existing configurations still work with the new flexible matching
Update documentation to reflect the more flexible naming convention

stories.headline: Configure streaming timeout for better connection handling
stories.summary: The new CLAUDE_STREAM_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS environment variable lets you customize how long Claude Code waits before timing out idle streaming connections. This helps prevent unnecessary disconnections during long-running operations.
actionable_steps: Choose a timeout value in milliseconds (default is 90000 for 90 seconds)
Restart Claude Code for the setting to take effect

stories.headline: Use environment variables to configure MCP server settings in Claude Code
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.85 introduced CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME and CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variables for MCP headersHelper scripts. This allows a single helper script to serve multiple MCP servers, simplifying configuration management.
actionable_steps: Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_NAME environment variable to your desired server name
Set the CLAUDE_CODE_MCP_SERVER_URL environment variable to your MCP server URL
Update your MCP headersHelper scripts to use these variables instead of hardcoded values
